Case Study — 02
MySensofar.

MySensofar is Sensofar's B2B client platform — used by distributors and customers worldwide to configure, quote and order precision metrology equipment. I ran two moderated usability tests and led the implementation of the resulting improvements.

Ongoing · Sensofar Tech

2022 – Present

UX Research & Writing

Moderated usability testing

The problem
Challenge
"The platform had grown organically, and several friction points had been flagged internally — but never validated with real users."
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Process
Step 01
Plan
Designed two moderated usability test scripts: one for the Help Center, one for the Sales module (configuration → quotation → approval). Defined realistic scenarios based on actual customer journeys.
2 test scripts Scenario design Task analysis
Step 02
Test
Ran moderated sessions with internal participants — sales staff, after-sales engineers and product specialists. Logged errors as critical or non-critical and captured think-aloud observations.
4 participants Think-aloud Error logging
Step 03
Implement
Translated findings into specific design and copy recommendations. Worked with the product team to prioritise and implement — all four improvements shipped within the same release cycle.
UX writing Design recommendations 4 shipped

"Users kept clicking 'Summary' expecting to review their selection — not realising it was the button to move forward. Several stopped and asked if they had missed a step."

— Observation, Sales module usability test
4 findings shipped
Finding 01 — Button label caused confusion

The primary action button was labelled "Summary" — users interpreted it as a read-only review, not a call to action. Renamed to "Continue" to communicate forward movement.

Before → After — button label
Finding 02 — Missing navigation context

The breadcrumb only showed the top-level section. Users inside a quotation had no way to know where they were. Adding the subsection level gave users back their location context.

Before — breadcrumb missing
After — location visible
Finding 03 — No feedback after key actions

Users completed key actions with no confirmation or next step. We introduced contextual snackbars — some informative, some with a direct link to the next section.

Contextual snackbars — success & informational
Finding 04 — Legibility issues on white backgrounds

Several UI elements had insufficient contrast on white backgrounds. We iterated on the colour palette to meet accessibility standards.

Contrast iteration — improved legibility
Outcomes
2
Moderated usability tests designed and run — Help Center and Sales module
4
UX improvements shipped: button label, navigation breadcrumb, snackbars, contrast
100%
Of key findings translated into shipped product changes within the same release cycle
